question: Volley executor pairing — Claude as implementer / Codex as auditor, or the reverse?
answer: Resolved pre-dispatch: Claude=implementer, Codex=auditor. No role swap on this first run. Reasons: (a) F005b's read-only sandbox is real on Codex (--sandbox read-only at OS level) but only matcher-restricted Read on Claude — Codex auditor can run pytest/git inspection; Claude auditor cannot. (c) Reduces variables for the first dogfood — pinning the pairing means deviations in volley behavior reflect orchestrator/dispatch issues, not pairing experiments. Will be invoked via `--implementer claude --auditor codex`.

question: Cost-guard activation for the run.
answer: Resolved pre-dispatch: cost-guard runs sentinel-inert for this dogfood. Reason per operator guidance 2026-04-29: do NOT edit the tracked config/cost_budgets.json to inject a temp budget — that creates a tracked-file mutation outside the dogfood's locked scope and risks pollution of the cost-guard surface for other consumers. If we want cost-guard telemetry post-run, the right path is `cost-guard --budgets <tmp-file>` against an out-of-tree budget file. For this run we accept that cost-guard emits `no_budgets_configured` throughout and rely on F006 budget_ceiling + F007 quota_admission as the actual runtime guards (which gate dispatch on real ~/.jarvis/quota_state.json data, not on cost-guard).

question: Auditor read-only sandbox tradeoff — Codex tempdir-creation behavior.
answer: Real-volley dispatch revealed a meaningful constraint on the F005b auditor read-only sandbox claim. Codex auditor (Codex CLI under `--sandbox read-only`) attempted to run `pytest` against the implementer's product but was blocked at collection time with `No usable temporary directory`. Codex correctly fell back to inspecting the implementer's recorded evidence (audit JSON, validation_performed, summary) rather than failing the audit. This tempers the earlier framing that 'Codex auditor can independently run pytest' — read-only sandbox blocks not just repo writes but also tempfile creation, which pytest needs even for read-only test runs (cache, .pytest_cache, etc.). Implication: this is NOT a blocker for the dogfood, but is a follow-up design item. Two paths: (a) provide a writable temp area while keeping the repo read-only (e.g., `--sandbox read-only` + bind-mounted writable /tmp) so the auditor can actually rerun tests; (b) redefine auditor responsibility as artifact inspection only (current de-facto behavior) and update F005b prompt templates to make this explicit so audits don't claim test reruns they didn't perform. Recommend (a) — auditor independence has higher trust value if it can actually execute tests. Open follow-up plan, not in scope here.
